cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, just taught the people a whole song about the LORD, the Rock. Now he recites every word of it so all the people can hear. And he's not up there by himself.

cards.question: Moses recites the song to Israel with someone beside him. Who is it?

cards.text: Joshua son of Nun, the man the LORD commissioned to bring Israel into the land (Deuteronomy 31:23). Moses finishes every last word of the song, and then he's got one more thing to say to all Israel.

cards.question: Moses tells all Israel to take his words to heart. Why does he say they should?

answers.text: So they can command their children to follow the law
So they can teach the law to the nations nearby
So they can carve the law on the city gates

cards.text: Moses says, "they are not idle words to you." In other words, this is NOT one of those warranty cards in my old junk drawer that nobody ever read.

cards.question: Moses says these words aren't idle. What does he say they are to Israel?
True or false: Moses says that by these words, Israel will live long in the land across the Jordan.

cards.text: On that same day, the LORD speaks to Moses. I bet Moses hasn't even caught his breath from that song yet.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to go up into the Abarim Range to Mount ___.

cards.text: Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, right across from Jericho. Friend, if the LORD told ME to climb a mountain, I'd be at the bottom on my gold base, hopping and yelling "ALMOST THERE" for a month.

cards.question: Once Moses is up on Mount Nebo, the LORD tells him to ___ the land of ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses something heavy. There on that mountain, Moses will die and be gathered to his people.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses he'll die on the mountain just like someone in his family did. Who?

cards.text: His brother Aaron, who died on Mount Hor. Then the LORD tells Moses why, and it goes back to the waters of Meribah-kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says only Aaron broke faith with Him at Meribah-kadesh.

cards.text: Both of them broke faith with Him, the LORD says, by failing to treat Him as holy in front of the Israelites. So what does that mean for Moses and the land?

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Moses he will see the land from a distance but will not enter it.

cards.text: That's a heavy day for Moses, friend. But his story's not over yet, so keep your apron on.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "they are not idle words to you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card describes the song as being 'about the LORD, the Rock.' That fact comes from Deuteronomy 32:4, which is outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it. The card only cites 32:44. Card 3 shows the fix: it gives its outside fact an inline reference (Deuteronomy 31:23).

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess how Moses finishes his line: 'They are your life' against 'crown' or 'shield.' Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason to 'life' over the other two. It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning. A better card could ask what the words do for Israel, or why they aren't idle, which the baker can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Story card 12 already tells the baker that Moses will die on the mountain across from the land, and card 11 has him viewing the land from there. Card 16 then sets up the question by asking what this means for Moses and the land. By then, 'he will see the land from a distance but will not enter it' is already given away. One fix is to make Moses' death on the mountain (32:50) the choice card instead of telling it on card 12, so that card 17 becomes an easy follow-up to an answered choice.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Outside the warranty-card line (card 5) and the mountain-climbing line (card 10), Papa Dorin reads as a pleasant dad rather than laugh-out-loud funny. 'I bet Moses hasn't even caught his breath from that song yet' (card 8) and 'keep your apron on' (card 18) are mild. The opening cards (1 to 4) have almost no voice. The moments before the news of Moses' death could hold a real laugh without muddying any fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
